# Random effects meta-analysis for correlated test statistics

  

  

![](reference/figures/image.png)

Meta-analysis is widely used to summarize estimated effects sizes across
multiple statistical tests. Standard fixed and random effect
meta-analysis methods assume that the estimates of the effect sizes are
statistically independent. Here we relax this assumption and enable
meta-analysis when the correlation matrix between effect size estimates
is known. Fixed effect meta-analysis uses the method of [Lin and
Sullivan (2009)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajhg.2009.11.001), and random
effects meta-analysis uses the method of [Han, et
al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1093/hmg/ddw049). An extension of the
Lin-Sullivan method for finite sample size is described in [Hoffman and
Roussos (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.01.29.635498).

## Usage

``` r
# Run fixed effects meta-analysis, 
#  accounting for correlation 
LS( beta, stders, Sigma)

# Run fixed effects meta-analysis, 
#  accounting for correlation,
#  and finite sample size using residual degrees of freedom
LS.empirical( beta, stders, Sigma, nu=rdf)

# Run random effects meta-analysis, 
#  accounting for correlation 
RE2C( beta, stders, Sigma)
```

## Install from GitHub

``` r
devtools::install_github("DiseaseNeurogenomics/remaCor")
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`LS()`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/LS.md) :
  Fixed effect meta-analysis for correlated test statistics
- [`LS.empirical()`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/LS.empirical.md)
  : Fixed effect meta-analysis for correlated test statistics
- [`RE2C()`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/RE2C.md)
  : Random effect meta-analysis for correlated test statistics
- [`hotelling()`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/hotelling.md)
  : Hottelling T^2 test for multivariate regression
- [`pkg.env`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/pkg.env.md)
  : Local environment
- [`plotCor()`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/plotCor.md)
  : Correlation plot
- [`plotForest()`](http://gabrielhoffman.github.io/remaCor/reference/plotForest.md)
  : Forest plot of coefficients
